title: Homogeneous character-line cohomology with its canonical left coaction
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $G,B$ be $F$-group schemes with $G$ affine and $i_B:B\to G$ a homomorphism [def-sc-group-scheme], let $Y$ be an $F$-scheme and $\pi:G\to Y$ an $F$-morphism, and let $\chi:B\to\mathbf G_m$ be a character. Define a character-line-cohomology presentation as the following data, without asserting existence. It contains an associated-character-line-bundle presentation $P$ for $(G,B,i_B,Y,\pi,\chi)$ [def-sfb-associated-character-line-bundle], with section sheaf $L$, atlas trivialization $\tau:\pi^*L\simeq\mathcal O_G$, and natural left action on $Y$, and a linearization $\ell$ of this action on $L$ [def-sfb-group-scheme-linearization]. Require that for every test $F$-scheme $Z$ and $s,g\in G(Z)$, the composite $\mathcal O_Z\xrightarrow{\tau_g^{-1}}(\pi g)^*L\xrightarrow{\ell_{s,\pi g}}(s\pi g)^*L$ equals $\tau_{sg}^{-1}$, with targets identified by $s\pi(g)=\pi(sg)$. For $i\ge0$, write $H^i(Y,L)$ for right-derived module global sections [pqf-def-cohomology], with its $F$-vector-space structure obtained by restricting the global-function scalars along $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}F$. The remaining data are coassociative counital coactions $c_i:H^i(Y,L)\to H^i(Y,L)\otimes_F F[G]$, using the actual coordinate Hopf algebra [def-sfb-rational-highest-weight-data]. They are required to be the natural cohomological action as follows. On $W=G\times_FY$ let $p_1,p_2$ be the projections and $a^-(g,y)=g^{-1}y$. Let $A_i:H^i(Y,L)\to H^i(W,p_2^*L)$ be the canonical cohomology map [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] for $a^-$ and the coefficient map adjoint to $\ell_{g^{-1},y}^{-1}:(a^-)^*L\to p_2^*L$. Let $P_i$ be the canonical cohomology pullback along $p_2$, using the ordinary pullback adjunction unit. For every finite tensor expression $c_i(z)=\sum_j v_j\otimes f_j$ require $A_i(z)=\sum_j p_1^*(f_j)\,P_i(v_j)$. Thus the canonical flat-base-change comparison, whose value on $v\otimes f$ is $p_1^*f\,p_2^*v$, carries $c_i$ to the universal left-translation action. This fixes the algebraic coaction, including after arbitrary commutative $F$-algebra extension, rather than specifying an arbitrary action or base-change isomorphism.
